records.decision_reason: LiteLLM maintainer statement and Wiz forensic analysis establish compromised release workflow, malicious packages and observed credential abuse.

severity_evidence.reason: Malicious releases distributed to multiple environments with observed theft and subsequent use of cloud credentials; exact victim count unknown.

records.title: LiteLLM release pipeline compromised with credential stealer
records.victim: LiteLLM open-source package and downstream installations
records.what: Attackers used compromised maintainer GitHub credentials to publish malicious LiteLLM 1.107.0 Python and Docker releases with a credential stealer. Wiz observed subsequent abuse of stolen AWS credentials.
records.significance: Compromised AI software distribution and theft of cloud and AI credentials; affected releases were removed within hours.

records.decision_reason: TfL disclosure confirms compromise and potentially exposed personal data affecting about 265,000 customers.

severity_evidence.reason: Approximately 265,000 customers potentially exposed; Oyster card travel remained operational and misuse was not established.

records.title: TfL Oyster photocard account breach affects about 265,000
records.victim: Transport for London Oyster photocard customers
records.what: TfL discovered compromised email/account infrastructure after fraudulent account-creation messages were sent from its systems. Personal data including names, addresses, dates of birth and security questions may have been exposed; the photocard portal was taken offline.
records.significance: Transport authority reported approximately 265,000 potentially affected accounts and suspended a customer portal while investigating.
